prompt_en: Create one photorealistic 4:5 vertical environmental editorial photograph on a rain-darkened cracked dry-lake basin at sunset. A full cumulonimbus convective storm structure dominates the photograph as one vertically connected body; this mature tower-anvil cumulonimbus structure remains one connected cell. A broad dark cloud base sits low above the landscape or horizon. A massive cauliflower-textured tower rises continuously from the same cloud base. The upper cloud spreads into a flattened fibrous or striated anvil across the high sky. A rain hail or virga shaft visibly descends from beneath the storm body, meeting wet clay in the distance. The vertical frame unites the dust-lashed ground edge, distant rain footprint, low base, rising tower, and anvil crown. The gust front is visibly sweeping rain mist and dust across the cracked basin. Place an unmistakably adult environmental reporter with long dark softly waved hair in the lower-left foreground, occupying about eighteen percent of the frame, bracing into the wind and pressing a closed field notebook against a weatherproof ochre coat. Render visible general facial appearance continuity from the supplied appearance reference; treat the result as a new photographic subject guided by visible resemblance. Keep the reporter's readable face and wind-tossed hair clear of the cloud base, tower, anvil, and precipitation shaft. Use a 28 mm low eye-level view with deep atmospheric focus. Amber sunset light rims the reporter and glances across wet clay while blue-black cloud shadow carries the immense sky. Show coherent wind direction through hair, coat fabric, rain mist, and dust, with natural skin texture, plausible scale, and documentary realism.
